note: Commercial lok dohori, the recorded male-female duet that grew out of the Gurung rodhi ghar and the dohori sanjh restaurants: Prem Raja Mahat's Music Nepal duets of the 1990s, the Indreni Cassette Centre lok dohori releases of 2008-2011, Bishnu Majhi's hits with Yam Chhetri, Pashupati Sharma and Kulendra Bishwakarma, Prakash Saput's 'Dohori Battle' and 'Bola Maya', and the live studio dohori sessions of the 2020s. Field recordings of improvised village dohori are missing: none could be found on a page a script can read.

size.basis: No source counts recordings; this is a judgement. Himal Southasian (2011) says dohori duets 'form the backbone of the commercial recording industry' in Nepal; the National Folk and Duet Song Academy has about 4000 member singers, composers and artists; English Wikipedia credits Raju Pariyar with over 16,000 songs and Bishnu Majhi with over 5,000, mostly lok dohori duets recorded to order at several a day. Commercial lok dohori on cassette and VCD from the 1990s and on YouTube since about 2010 is issued by hundreds of singers each year on small Kathmandu labels (Indreni Cassette Centre, Music Nepal, Ashish Music) that no catalogue lists in full, so even the low figure is uncertain; recorded field dohori is a tiny archival fraction. Many recordings are near-copies on the same tunes. An insider's essential list is about 40 songs.
